raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for as long as I can remember. I have about 8 mu of contracted land. There's really no question about what I'll grow — everyone around here grows winter wheat and summer corn. That's how we've always done it, and it makes sense: the wheat goes in after autumn, the corn follows right after harvest. Two crops a year off the same ground.

For the wheat, I'll go to the seed cooperative and buy Jimai 22 — it's what most people in the village use now. Better than the old varieties. I'll spread compound fertilizer before plowing, then add urea at jointing. I'll irrigate at sowing time if the soil is dry, then again before the ground freezes, then at jointing and heading. Four times should be enough. I'll spray once for weeds in early spring and once more if I see aphids or rust.

For the corn, I plant right after wheat harvest — no time to waste in June. I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, same as last year. No need to plow deep, just rotary till and seed. Corn needs less work but I'll top-dress with urea at the big bell stage. Maybe two irrigations if summer rains are short.

I won't change much from last year. Prices are okay and my body can still handle the work, though it gets harder every season.
